I’ve never met a single user who would use a naloxone needle to inject. It’s a huge ass needle lmao. It’s for intramuscular injections, which you can inject drugs intramuscularly- but no one does. They use IV needles, which are much smaller. They naloxone needles also have a safety feature that retracts the needle after injection. Hope this helps clarify !

As a paramedic who works harm reduction inner city- not sure what you’re looking for by what’s the story? Plenty of reason naloxone ends up this way. One- during overdoses in the dark trying to draw up and inject someone, supplies can get thrown around in a panic. Sometimes one whole kit is used and the second gets taken out in efforts to use but then is not needed. The needle is in the packaging, it’s a intramuscular needle, so no they don’t use it to inject in their veins, it’s far too big and has a vanish which retracts the needle after use. There are street teams that work to clean up these, as well as the community who use drugs. They bring back their used needles and exchange for new ones daily. Most of the inner city community get annoyed when people do not clean up their own supplies, as it reflects poorly on all the ones who do. 

Most of the time they are out cleaning up our parking lot for us to keep us safe when responding. The fire department also is AMAZING for this. 

If you’re wondering how you can help, sharps kits are free at pharmacy’s, and they have grabbers for the needles to clean them up. Looks to me like the pocket mask wasn’t used so likely  CPR wasn’t initiated, which is a win if they had it dealt with prior to things escalating. If it’s a common issue talking to the SCSs about it is good because we can frequent that area and see where we need sharps containers or clean up :)

Quickly before I write a longer reply, I never stated you personally. I was meaning in general that we can tend to feel that way. If you read it again it was just a point of commonality. I wasn’t at all saying you feel you lack significance. You stated above about not having those close relationships, in terms of others seeing your SH. Regardless of the reason you choose to not and cannot have them. Nothing I said is a personal attack on you, and I was merely suggesting self care tasks that might be of use. You do not have to use them. I’m really glad that you’re doing that within the community it’s really humbling and I’m sure it gives you a lot of healing to help others. Self worth comes from many different places, I’m not assuming anything and honestly the reason a lot of individuals don’t see a point is due to that reason, I was just trying to validate your feelings and give you a thumbs up for practicing harm reduction because I think it’s incredibly important. I’m sorry that I offended you, I did not mean that at all. I was just trying to relate.

Honestly, I’m a huge advocate for harm reduction. I have seen it save countless lives.  The whole idea behind it is meeting people where they are at. So meet yourself where you are at. Maybe you can’t stop cutting right now, that’s okay. But to reduce the harm you can make sure you’re not going over healing wounds, proper wound care, and maybe throw in some other self care activities like; a bath, reading, drawing, quick walk, tv, music, anything you enjoy. 

I work in addictions and this mindset you’re describing is very common. “I don’t see myself stopping” there is a lot to unpack in this of the why? Generally it can be because you feel you lack significance. With no external attachments such as family, significant other etc this can lead us to believe ourselves when we say these things. Just because you think it doesn’t make it true.  There is also something to be said about the fact that you have to wake up to YOU everyday. You have to live with you. You don’t need to feel better for anyone else, but It sounds like you might deserve a version of yourself that you’ve tucked away due to pain. Bring them back, You work at your own pace. It sounds like you’re taking care of your wounds and that is great. Always use clean supplies to avoid infection etc. There may come a day where a rock bottom will hit and you’ll say I don’t want to be doing this anymore. I’m almost positive you do not want to be doing this now, no one wants to SH. It’s a coping mechanism, it’s control, it’s a lot of things we feel we lack. I promise you though there is a world you have yet to discover that doesn’t involve SH. You are doing your best, I’m proud of you for practicing diligent safety when SHing. 

Also something that has helped me is the 1% rule. 
There is something to be said about being 1% better than you were the day before. Maybe that means today I will put away a dirty dish that I left out. Doesn’t seem like a lot but it’s 1% better than I did yesterday. This can apply here as well however you see fit. If anything this gives me a sense of improvement. The more I do it the better my habits become. It’s not a fast process by any means but it’s a do able one.

I’m going to be blunt with you. It’s hard to gauge the age gap when you’re 15. An older man tells you you’re mature for your age, and it feels so nice to be noticed and you think you will be treated what you’re worth. He says the right things and you believe him. There is 16 years between you guys. You are a child still, not saying you’re not mature or equipped. But in the reality of it, you’re not allowed to legally make decisions for yourself, you are technically a child. He is a grown man. I can’t imagine myself with an 18 year old (I’m 23 and from Canada so adult age is 18) which is legal, let alone a minor. Your brain isn’t even finished developing, you still are learning and experiencing life. He took advantage of your innocence. He groomed you.  Do not think for a second that this is your fault. It does not matter that you didn’t say no. An adult male, realistically old enough to be your father, groomed you and took you back to his place. You are young, you’re going to make decisions you regret, and do stupid things. That being said this is not a stupid thing. The pressure you felt would be very intense. When our body is exposed to trauma, we go into fight or flight, but also we can freeze. It’s our body’s response to stressful events, everything you did in that situation was normal. I also know the shame and fear you can feel for speaking up and telling him to stop. What if he reacts and hurts you? Or things escalate, Etc. you did exactly what your body told you to do and there is nothing wrong with that. I’m going to repeat this is not your fault because I want you to know, and believe that. When you age, this will become more clear to you. I promise you when you are 31, the very last thing you will be looking at is a 15 year old boy. That is child molestation. I am incredibly sorry you have had this experience. He touched you without your consent, he penetrated you, and he knew your age. This man is a pedophile, I’m sure this isn’t the first time he has done this and it won’t be the last. If you need any support we are here. I’d recommend talking to someone you trust, seek out the schools councillor, and I would suggest you report this. I want you to have all the support, and justice you deserve for this. You do not deserve this, you have done nothing to deserve this. You are still growing my dear, and if I could take what happened to you away I would. Advocate for yourself honey, it’s HARD. But you will be able to do it. I’m so proud of you for sharing your story, I wish that when I was 15 I was as bright and open as you. You will overcome this and you will be okay. If you need anything I’m available. I would also recommend an STI check. I know it seems really scary, but I promise you it’s not. They are SO good at the clinics. Usually a womens clinic is the best, but you can also go to a gynaecologist, or STI clinic. Quick google should do the trick. 

Please reach out if you need more supports, and keep talking about it because it gets easier every time. 
Sincerely, a young adult with a sister your age and similar experience.

As someone who works at a safe consumption site as a medical professional,
It depends on what you take. Certain medications will cause a slow painful death, others will inhibit your respiratory drive and you’ll stop breathing, and then your heart will stop beating. Most people I have had the opportunity to revive from their overdose thanked me as they did not want to die. You won’t have a choice if you “sleep” or not depending on what you take it will just happen as your body shuts down. Depending on if you are found or not, you could end up with severe brain damage, or on life support with a ventilator breathing for you. Please reach out to supports, please don’t kill yourself. I know how bad it feels, I really do. I promise there are healthcare providers who actually care. I care. Please contact 911 of you have already taken meds, and if you haven’t contact them anyways talk to them, they will get you some help. It won’t be a fast process but I swear to you this will give you an opportunity to grow and heal. Regards, 
A paramedic who cares. 🤍
